title: The task
body: Seven problem statements, none of which names a pattern. For each one, find the **signal** in the wording and the limits, then name the pattern and its time. This is the first thing to do in an interview, before any code.

title: Problem 1
body: “A sorted list of prices: find two that add up to exactly 50.” The signal is **sorted + a pair**, which points to **two pointers**.

vars.name: problem
vars.value: A sorted list of prices: find two that add up to exactly 50.

title: Problem 2
body: “The longest run of days with at most 2 rainy days.” The signal is **contiguous + at most k**, which points to **sliding window**.

vars.name: problem
vars.value: The longest run of days with at most 2 rainy days.

title: Problem 3
body: “The fewest moves for a knight to reach a square.” The signal is **fewest steps, equal cost**, which points to **BFS**.

vars.name: problem
vars.value: The fewest moves for a knight to reach a square.

predict.question: “The fewest moves for a knight to reach a square.” Which pattern fits?
options: BFS: fewest steps where every move costs the same
DFS: explore as deep as possible first
predict.explanation: Fewest steps with equal-cost moves is shortest path in an unweighted graph, so BFS level by level.

title: Problem 4
body: “List every way to choose 3 of 10 toppings.” The signal is **list all choices**, which points to **backtracking**.

vars.name: problem
vars.value: List every way to choose 3 of 10 toppings.

title: Problem 5
body: “The slowest reading speed that finishes a book list in 8 hours.” The signal is **smallest value that works; works stays true as it grows**, which points to **binary search on the answer**.

vars.name: problem
vars.value: The slowest reading speed that finishes a book list in 8 hours.

vars.name: signal
vars.value: smallest value that works; works stays true as it grows

predict.question: “The slowest reading speed that finishes in 8 hours.” Which pattern fits?
options: Sort the books and read the longest first
predict.explanation: If a speed works, every faster speed also works. That yes/no line can be binary searched.

title: Problem 6
body: “The number of ways to make 100 cents from coins.” The signal is **count ways; choices overlap**, which points to **dynamic programming**.

vars.name: problem
vars.value: The number of ways to make 100 cents from coins.

title: Problem 7
body: “For each day, how many days until a warmer one.” The signal is **next greater to the right**, which points to **monotonic stack**. Done: seven statements, seven signals. With practice the signal jumps out before you think about code.

vars.value: For each day, how many days until a warmer one.
